key_insight: MANTA lets a multi-agent system adapt its communication topology during inference, so the collaboration structure can self-evolve when the current setup is no longer effective.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for building more robust agentic systems because it suggests topology, not just prompts or policies, can be adjusted online to improve task performance without changing the agent budget.
method: Initialize a task-conditioned network topology from prior structural experience.
Monitor collaboration traces during execution and trigger bounded structural updates when needed.
Adapt roles, links, execution order, visibility, and validation paths while preserving the task interface.
evidence_signal: Across five benchmarks spanning information seeking, tool use, planning, workflow execution, and mathematical reasoning, MANTA achieved a 74.0 average score and beat the strongest baseline by 5.8 points, with the best result on PlanCraft.
watch_item: Because the method changes communication structure online, its stability, overhead, and failure modes under noisy traces or tight latency constraints need careful implementation and evaluation.
paper_title: MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
